verses.1: David rose and went to the city. Jonathan came to the city.
verses.2: David went to Nob, to Ahimelech the priest. Ahimelech trembled at the sight of David and asked him, "Why are you alone, and no one is with you?"
verses.3: David said to the priest Ahimelech, "The king has commanded me with something and said to me, 'No man must know the matter about which I am sending you and the one about whom I have given you orders. I have told the boys to go to a certain place, Almoni.'"
verses.4: "Now, is there anything at all under your hand? Give me five loaves of bread, or whatever is found."
verses.5: The priest answered David and said, "There are no common loaves under my hand, for there are only sacred loaves. If the boys have been kept from a woman, then they may be eaten."
verses.6: David answered the priest and said to him, "Indeed, a woman was kept from us only yesterday and today when I came out on the road. The boys’ vessels are holy, and the road is common. Even today the vessels will be considered holy."
verses.7: The priest gave David the sacred bread, for there was no other bread there, only the bread of the Presence that had been removed from before the LORD to be put in place of the hot bread when it was taken away.
verses.8: There was a man from the servants of Saul present that day, detained before the LORD. His name was Doeg the Edomite, a herdsman for Saul.
verses.9: David said to Ahimelech, "Is there a spear or sword at all under your hand? For I have not taken my sword or my weapons with me, because the king's command was urgent."
verses.10: The priest said, "The sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you struck down in the Valley of Elah—there it is, wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod. If you take it, take it, for there is none other like it here." David said, "There is none like it. Let me have it."
verses.11: David rose and fled that day from the face of Saul, and he went to Achish, king of Gath.
verses.12: The servants of Achish said to him, "Is this not David, the king of the land? Is it not for this that they used to sing in the dances, 'Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his ten thousands'?"
verses.13: David put these words to himself in his heart and was greatly afraid of Achish, king of Gath.
verses.14: He changed his behavior before them and behaved foolishly in their sight, and he acted like a madman, shaking his hands and feet, and drooling down his beard.
verses.15: Achish said to his servants, "Look, I see a man who is mad. Why have you brought him to me?"
verses.16: "I am short of madmen," said Achish, "that you have brought this one to me to make me mad? Shall this man enter my house?"

notes:
Notes
- v. 3: "Almoni" is a place name, translated from פְּלֹנִי אַלְמוֹנִי, where פְּלֹנִי ("certain") is a common placeholder in Hebrew texts, and "Almoni" is the specific place.
- v. 10: "wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod" is an interpretive rendering of the Hebrew phrase אַחֲרֵי הָאֵפוֹד, which literally means "after the ephod," but the context implies location.
- v. 13: "Drooling down his beard" is a natural rendering of the Hebrew "riro" (רִירוֹ), referring to the act of drooling, and "zakan" (זְקָנֽוֹ) meaning beard.

[1] David rose and went to the city. Jonathan came to the city.

[2] David went to Nob, to Ahimelech the priest. Ahimelech trembled at the sight of David and asked him, "Why are you alone, and no one is with you?"

[3] David said to the priest Ahimelech, "The king has commanded me with something and said to me, 'No man must know the matter about which I am sending you and the one about whom I have given you orders. I have told the boys to go to a certain place, Almoni.'"

[4] "Now, is there anything at all under your hand? Give me five loaves of bread, or whatever is found."

[5] The priest answered David and said, "There are no common loaves under my hand, for there are only sacred loaves. If the boys have been kept from a woman, then they may be eaten."

[6] David answered the priest and said to him, "Indeed, a woman was kept from us only yesterday and today when I came out on the road. The boys’ vessels are holy, and the road is common. Even today the vessels will be considered holy."

[7] The priest gave David the sacred bread, for there was no other bread there, only the bread of the Presence that had been removed from before the LORD to be put in place of the hot bread when it was taken away.

[8] There was a man from the servants of Saul present that day, detained before the LORD. His name was Doeg the Edomite, a herdsman for Saul.

[9] David said to Ahimelech, "Is there a spear or sword at all under your hand? For I have not taken my sword or my weapons with me, because the king's command was urgent."

[10] The priest said, "The sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you struck down in the Valley of Elah—there it is, wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod. If you take it, take it, for there is none other like it here." David said, "There is none like it. Let me have it."

[11] David rose and fled that day from the face of Saul, and he went to Achish, king of Gath.

[12] The servants of Achish said to him, "Is this not David, the king of the land? Is it not for this that they used to sing in the dances, 'Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his ten thousands'?"

[13] David put these words to himself in his heart and was greatly afraid of Achish, king of Gath.

[14] He changed his behavior before them and behaved foolishly in their sight, and he acted like a madman, shaking his hands and feet, and drooling down his beard.

[15] Achish said to his servants, "Look, I see a man who is mad. Why have you brought him to me?"

[16] "I am short of madmen," said Achish, "that you have brought this one to me to make me mad? Shall this man enter my house?"
